title: London System
intro: d4, Nf3 and Bf4, then e3, c3 and Nbd2: one calm, solid set-up for White against almost anything.

lessons.title: The London set-up
lessons.summary: Bishop out first, then a rock-solid pawn triangle.

steps.text: The London System puts the dark-squared bishop on f4 early, before e3 locks it in. Then White builds a solid triangle of pawns on c3, d4 and e3.
Play the London: d4, Nf3, then the bishop to f4.
steps.hint: Queen's pawn, king's knight, then the bishop goes out before e3.
steps.ifWrong: The London goes d4, Nf3, Bf4.
steps.ifRight: The bishop is out before the pawns close it in.

steps.text: Support d4 and open a path for your other bishop.
steps.hint: A one-square pawn move in front of the king.
steps.ifRight: d4 is supported and the f1 bishop can come out.

steps.text: Black adds pressure on d4 with 4...Nc6.
Develop the queen's knight to d2, where it does not block the c-pawn.
steps.hint: On c3 the knight would stop your c-pawn moving.
steps.ifWrong: In the London the knight goes to d2, keeping c3 free for a pawn.
The triangle needs a pawn on c3.
steps.ifRight: c3, d4, e3: the London fortress. Next come Bd3 and castling.

steps.text: Black offers to trade bishops with ...Bd6. London players usually keep their bishop. Where does it go?
steps.hint: Step back along the diagonal, still eyeing Black's queenside.
steps.ifWrong: Keep the bishop by stepping back to g3.
steps.ifRight: The bishop stays, and if Black takes on g3, your h-pawn takes back.

feedback.f4d6: Trading is fine too. Most London players keep the bishop with Bg3.
